name: LIST 5
description: Combined tasks: each item chains several steps (data, formulas, compile, fit, graph, 3D, notes) and reuses what earlier items created (see README.md).
instruction: Use exactly the object names given. End the item by printing exactly ONE line: the result label the item gives, then only the values asked for, in the order asked, separated by spaces.

items.text: Create a table "Calib" with 21 rows and three columns: "x" (role X) = 0, 0.1, ..., 2; "y" (role Y) given by a column formula 3*x^2 - 2*x + 1 recalculated in the default scripting language; "dy" (role yErr) = 0.05 everywhere. Compile a new fit function "ai/Quad" for y = a*x^2 + b*x + c with all three parameters adjustable, and fit it to "Calib" weighted by dy, starting from a = b = c = 1. Print a, b and c with 4 decimals, and the number of rows where y is greater than 5.
items.hint: ^ in the Python column formula or in the C++ code, the fit unweighted, the y name of the compiled function, or the count taken from the fit instead of the table
items.verify:
t = table("Calib")
check(t.numRows(), existTable("fitCurve-ai/Quad"), sum(1 for v in t.colData(2) if v > 5))

items.text: Create a table "Peak5" with 81 rows: x = -4, -3.9, ..., 4 and y = 2/(1 + (x/0.5)^2) + 0.1 (roles X, Y). Compile two new fit functions, "ai/Gauss5" for y = A*exp(-x^2/(2*w^2)) + c and "ai/Lor5" for y = A/(1 + (x/w)^2) + c, each with A, w and c adjustable. Fit both to "Peak5", each starting from A = 1, w = 1, c = 0. Print the name of the function with the smaller chi2/dof, then its fitted A and w (as a positive number), each with 4 decimals.
items.hint: the second fit's chi2/dof compared with itself, the parameters of the other model printed, or ^ in the C++ code

items.text: Create a graph "Report5" with two stacked layers: the top one with the "Calib" y data as points and the fitted curve from table "fitCurve-ai/Quad" as a line, the bottom one with that table's residuals. Set the Y axis title of the top layer to "y" and the X axis title of the bottom layer to "x". Print the number of layers, the number of curves in the top and in the bottom layer, and the largest absolute residual with 4 decimals.
items.hint: one layer only, the fit curve rebuilt instead of taken from fitCurve-ai/Quad, or the residuals read from the wrong column
items.verify:
gw = graphWindow("Report5")
top, bottom = gw.layer(1), gw.layer(2)
fromFit = lambda l: any(l.curveTitle(i).startswith("fitCurve-ai/Quad_") for i in range(l.numCurves()))
check(gw.numLayers(), top.numCurves(), bottom.numCurves(), fromFit(top), fromFit(bottom))

items.text: Create a 21x21 matrix "Saddle" spanning x and y from -1 to 1 and fill it with x*x - y*y. Plot it as a 3D surface in a window named "Saddle3D". Print the value at the centre of the matrix (row 11, column 11), the smallest and the largest value of all cells, and whether a 3D window "Saddle3D" exists.
items.hint: the coordinates not set (formula over the cell indices), the 3D window looked up with graphWindow(), or its name not set
items.verify:
m = matrix("Saddle")
check(existPlot3D("Saddle3D"), m.numRows(), m.numCols(), m.cell(11, 11))

items.text: Create a note "Pipeline" with two tabs named "make" and "check" (the first tab renamed too). The "make" tab holds a script that creates a table "Auto" with 5 rows whose column 1 is 1, 2, ..., 5; the "check" tab holds a script that prints the sum of column 1 of "Auto". Run only the "make" tab. Print the number of tabs, whether table "Auto" exists, and the sum of its column 1.
items.hint: the tab never run, both tabs run, the table created directly instead of through the tab, or renameTab() given a 1-based index

items.text: Delete the fit functions "ai/Quad", "ai/Gauss5" and "ai/Lor5" from the library, and close and delete the table "Peak5" and the note "Pipeline". Print which of the three function names still exist (a list, [] if none), then whether "Peak5" and "Pipeline" still exist.
items.hint: delete() called without Compiler, a misspelled name, or a window hidden instead of deleted
items.verify: check([f for f in ("ai/Quad", "ai/Gauss5", "ai/Lor5") if Compiler.functionExists(f)], existTable("Peak5"), existNote("Pipeline"))
